scope: US DailyMed primary prescribing labels; target flags mean explicit naming in section 12.1, not absence of biological activity when false. DailyMed update dates differ from prescribing-information revision dates.

drugs.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2012; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
drugs.approved_indications_summary: Advanced renal cell carcinoma: first line with avelumab or pembrolizumab; monotherapy after one prior systemic therapy fails.
drugs.target_mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR1, VEGFR2 and VEGFR3 at therapeutic plasma concentrations; PDGFRA is not named in section 12.1.
drugs.hepatic_safety_summary: Section 5.11 warns of liver-enzyme elevations with monotherapy and increased frequency of grade 3–4 ALT/AST elevations with avelumab or pembrolizumab. Liver tests require monitoring; severe combination-associated hepatotoxicity can require interruption, corticosteroids or permanent discontinuation. No hepatic boxed warning.
drugs.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Cancer approval and kinase inhibition do not establish efficacy or safety for liver fibrosis; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

drugs.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2021; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
drugs.approved_indications_summary: Adults with relapsed or refractory advanced renal cell carcinoma after at least two systemic therapies.
drugs.target_mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR1/2/3 phosphorylation, c-KIT and PDGFR-beta at clinically relevant concentrations; PDGFRA is not named.
drugs.hepatic_safety_summary: No dedicated hepatotoxicity warning or boxed warning in this label. TIVO-3 laboratory abnormalities include ALT elevation (30%; grade 3–4, 4%), AST elevation (28%; grade 3–4, 1%), and bilirubin elevation (11%; grade 3–4, 3%). Dose adjustment applies to moderate hepatic impairment; severe impairment is to be avoided.
drugs.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Absence of a dedicated warning is not evidence of hepatic safety; no liver-fibrosis indication or efficacy is established by this label.

drugs.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2015; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
drugs.approved_indications_summary: Progressive, recurrent/metastatic radioactive-iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer; advanced renal cell carcinoma with pembrolizumab first line or everolimus after one antiangiogenic therapy; unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma first line; advanced pMMR/non-MSI-H endometrial carcinoma with pembrolizumab after systemic therapy progression when curative surgery/radiation is unsuitable.
drugs.target_mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR1/2/3; label explicitly identifies VEGFR3 as FLT4 and includes PDGFRA, FGFR1–4, KIT and RET.
drugs.hepatic_safety_summary: Section 5.4 hepatotoxicity warning includes serious and fatal hepatic events. Liver monitoring is required; grade 3–4 toxicity may require withholding/discontinuation and hepatic failure requires discontinuation. No hepatic boxed warning.
drugs.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Hepatocellular carcinoma approval does not establish antifibrotic efficacy or suitability for nonmalignant liver disease; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

drugs.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2006; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
drugs.approved_indications_summary: Adult GIST after imatinib progression/intolerance; advanced renal cell carcinoma; adjuvant therapy after nephrectomy for high-risk recurrent RCC; progressive, well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors with unresectable locally advanced/metastatic disease.
drugs.target_mechanism: Inhibits PDGFR-alpha/beta, VEGFR1/2/3, KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R and RET.
drugs.hepatic_safety_summary: Boxed hepatotoxicity warning: hepatic injury can be severe or fatal. Hepatic monitoring and interruption, dose reduction or discontinuation are specified; section 5.1 describes liver failure/death.
drugs.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Oncology approval and receptor inhibition do not establish antifibrotic benefit or acceptable safety in liver fibrosis; no such indication is listed.

drugs.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2009; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
drugs.approved_indications_summary: Adults with advanced renal cell carcinoma or advanced soft-tissue sarcoma after prior chemotherapy. Efficacy in adipocytic sarcoma or GIST is not established.
drugs.target_mechanism: Multikinase inhibitor including VEGFR1/2/3, PDGFR-alpha/beta, FGFR1/3, KIT, ITK, LCK and c-FMS.
drugs.hepatic_safety_summary: Boxed hepatotoxicity warning for severe and fatal hepatic toxicity. Baseline and ongoing liver monitoring and withholding, dose reduction or discontinuation according to severity are required.
drugs.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Oncology approval and receptor inhibition do not establish antifibrotic efficacy; hepatic toxicity is particularly relevant to repurposing for liver disease. No liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

drugs.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2005; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
drugs.approved_indications_summary: Unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma; advanced renal cell carcinoma; progressive, locally recurrent/metastatic differentiated thyroid carcinoma refractory to radioactive iodine.
drugs.target_mechanism: Inhibits RAF-family and cell-surface kinases including VEGFR1/2/3, KIT, FLT3, RET and PDGFR-beta. PDGFRA is not named.
drugs.hepatic_safety_summary: Section 5.10 warns of drug-induced hepatocellular injury, potentially causing liver failure or death; severe injury occurred in 2/3357 patients in a global monotherapy database. Regular liver tests and discontinuation for significant unexplained transaminase elevations are specified. No hepatic boxed warning.
drugs.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Hepatocellular carcinoma approval does not establish antifibrotic efficacy or safety for nonmalignant liver disease; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

drugs.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2012; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
drugs.approved_indications_summary: Adults with previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer (fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin/irinotecan, anti-VEGF and, if RAS wild-type, anti-EGFR therapy); advanced unresectable/metastatic GIST after imatinib and sunitinib; hepatocellular carcinoma after sorafenib.
drugs.target_mechanism: Regorafenib and/or active metabolites inhibit multiple kinases, explicitly including VEGFR3 and PDGFR-alpha, at clinically achieved concentrations.
drugs.hepatic_safety_summary: Boxed hepatotoxicity warning for severe and sometimes fatal hepatic toxicity. Baseline and ongoing liver monitoring plus interruption, reduction or discontinuation according to severity/persistence are specified. Hepatic warning updated February 2026.
drugs.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Hepatocellular carcinoma approval does not establish antifibrotic efficacy or safety for nonmalignant liver disease; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

drugs.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2012. Newly diagnosed Ph+ ALL combination indication has accelerated approval.
drugs.approved_indications_summary: Adults: newly diagnosed Ph+ ALL with chemotherapy; Ph+ ALL monotherapy when other kinase inhibitors are unsuitable or T315I-positive; CP-CML after resistance/intolerance to at least two kinase inhibitors; AP/BP-CML when other kinase inhibitors are unsuitable; T315I-positive CML. Not recommended for newly diagnosed CP-CML.
drugs.target_mechanism: Inhibits ABL and T315I-mutant ABL. Label names VEGFR/PDGFR families among additional targets but does not specify VEGFR3/FLT4 or PDGFRA isoforms.
drugs.hepatic_safety_summary: Boxed warning includes hepatotoxicity, liver failure and death, alongside arterial/venous vascular events and heart failure. Liver-test monitoring and interruption or discontinuation according to severity are specified.
drugs.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Family-level label target information cannot independently establish binding to either requested isoform; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed, and oncology approval does not establish antifibrotic benefit.
